Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 109, verse 1:

(p-687) Surah "al-Kafirun" (The Disbelievers)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: O you who disbelieve,﴾ the ones addressed are specific disbelievers. Allah already knew that they would not believe. It is related that "a group of the Quraysh said: 'O Muhammad, come, follow our religion and we will follow yours. You worship our gods for a year, and we will worship your God for a year.' He said: 'I seek refuge in Allah from associating anyone with Allah.' They said: 'Then touch some of our gods (istalim, i.e., touch/kiss them as a sign of acceptance), and we will believe you and worship your God.' So it was revealed. He went out to the Masjid al-Haram, where the chiefs of the Quraysh were present, and recited it to them, and they despaired."
Surah 109, verse 2: ﴿I do not worship what you worship.﴾ That is, I am not, in my present state, one who worships what you worship.

﴿Nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 5], the Hour.

﴿What I worship﴾: meaning Allah.
﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you worship﴾, and I will not worship, in the time that lies ahead of me, what you have worshipped.

Wa-la antum ʿabidūna mā aʿbud: the verse is rendered here as the Qur'an's words, with the phrase "ʿābidūna mā aʿbud" retained for discussion.

Translation:

﴿And neither are you worshippers of what I worship﴾, concerning what you are facing (currently),

﴿worshippers of what I worship﴾. He used the word "mā" (what), because what is intended by it is an attribute, meaning: "I do not worship falsehood, and you do not worship the Truth." Or, he used the word "mā" so that the two expressions would correspond (yatakābal al-lafẓān), and "man" (who) could not be used in the first clause while "mā" (what) is correct in the second, in the sense of "alladhī" (that which).

"لَكم دِينُكم ولِي دِينِ" ﴿To you is your religion, and to me is my religion﴾. Your religion means your shirk (associating partners with God), and my religion means my tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness). The reading with a fatha on the ya' (ولِيَ) is that of Nafi' and Hafs.

It is narrated that Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) entered the mosque while the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting, and he (ﷺ) said to him: "Nābidh (cast off), O Ibn Mas'ud." So he recited: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾. Then in the second rak'ah he (ﷺ) said to him: "Akhlis (be sincere)," so he recited: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾. When he finished the prayer, he (ﷺ) said: "O Ibn Mas'ud, ask, and you will be given."
